q-urgeschichte-21#explanation: Small groups moved via the Near East into Asia and reached Europe about 45,000 years ago.
q-urgeschichte-22#question: Where was the 1856 find made that gave the Neanderthals their name?
q-urgeschichte-22#choices.1: In a cave in the Swabian Jura
q-urgeschichte-22#choices.2: In a gravel pit near Heidelberg
q-urgeschichte-22#choices.3: In a cave in the Dordogne
q-urgeschichte-22#explanation: The bones from the Neander Valley gave the species its name; Neanderthals lived from Europe to Siberia and the Near East.
q-urgeschichte-23#question: About how many years ago did the Neanderthals die out?
q-urgeschichte-23#explanation: They vanished a few millennia after Homo sapiens reached Europe; around 400,000 years ago, by contrast, they had only just emerged.
q-urgeschichte-24#question: What does analysis of the DNA of present-day people outside Africa show?
q-urgeschichte-24#choices.1: They carry a large share of Homo erectus DNA
q-urgeschichte-24#choices.2: They carry no DNA at all from other human species
q-urgeschichte-24#choices.3: They carry a small share of Neanderthal DNA
q-urgeschichte-24#explanation: As they spread, modern humans occasionally interbred with Neanderthals; their share of the genome today amounts to a few percent.
q-urgeschichte-25#question: Which adaptation do many Tibetans owe to a gene variant inherited from the Denisovans?
q-urgeschichte-25#explanation: The gene variant makes life with little oxygen easier; people in New Guinea and Australia even carry up to five percent Denisovan DNA.
q-urgeschichte-26#question: What is the settlement of Australia at least 50,000 years ago early evidence of?
q-urgeschichte-26#explanation: Even with low sea levels, the ancestors of the Aboriginal Australians had to cross the sea from Southeast Asia by boat or raft.
q-urgeschichte-27#question: Which of these continents did Homo sapiens reach last?
q-urgeschichte-27#explanation: People reached America via the Bering land bridge at least 15,000, probably more than 20,000 years ago, long after Australia (at least 50,000 years ago) and Europe (about 45,000 years ago).
q-urgeschichte-28#question: Which ivory figure, about 40,000 years old, was found in the Swabian Jura?
q-urgeschichte-28#explanation: The Lion Man from the Hohlenstein-Stadel cave combines human and lion features and, together with the Venus of Hohle Fels, is among the oldest figurative artworks in the world.
q-urgeschichte-29#question: What are the oldest known musical instruments in the world?
q-urgeschichte-29#explanation: Flutes about 40,000 years old, made of vulture bone and mammoth ivory, were found in caves of the Swabian Jura.
q-urgeschichte-30#question: What do archaeologists conclude from healed bone fractures in Stone Age people?
q-urgeschichte-30#choices.0: That the injured were usually left behind
q-urgeschichte-30#choices.1: That the sick and injured were cared for by the group
q-urgeschichte-30#choices.2: That there were hardly any hunting accidents
q-urgeschichte-30#choices.3: That fractures were treated with metal splints
q-urgeschichte-30#explanation: Anyone who survived a serious injury depended on the help of others for weeks; Neanderthals, too, cared for their sick.
q-urgeschichte-31#question: Why did differences in wealth remain small among hunter-gatherers?
q-urgeschichte-31#choices.0: A chief distributed all goods equally
q-urgeschichte-31#choices.2: They could carry hardly any possessions on their travels
q-urgeschichte-31#choices.3: They did not yet know barter
q-urgeschichte-31#explanation: Only with settled life could stores, fields, herds and houses be accumulated and inherited; richly furnished graves then appear in the Neolithic.
q-urgeschichte-32#question: What do the skeletons of early farmers show compared with those of hunter-gatherers?
q-urgeschichte-32#choices.1: More tooth decay, wear and deficiency diseases
q-urgeschichte-32#choices.2: Hardly any traces of heavy physical labour
q-urgeschichte-32#explanation: A one-sided grain diet and heavy field work took their toll on health; in addition, dense settlements and close contact with livestock encouraged infectious diseases.
q-urgeschichte-33#question: Why did the number of children rise in Neolithic farming villages?
q-urgeschichte-33#choices.0: Women no longer had to work in the fields
q-urgeschichte-33#choices.1: Grain porridge shortened the breastfeeding period
q-urgeschichte-33#choices.3: Chiefs rewarded families with many children
q-urgeschichte-33#explanation: With porridge as food for small children, mothers could wean earlier and have children at shorter intervals; as a result the population grew markedly.
q-urgeschichte-34#question: Which plant was among the first crops in the Fertile Crescent?
q-urgeschichte-34#explanation: Besides emmer wheat, einkorn, barley and lentils were grown there; maize and potatoes come from the Americas, rice from Asia.
q-urgeschichte-35#question: In which region did farming arise independently of the Fertile Crescent?
q-urgeschichte-35#explanation: In China millet and rice were domesticated independently; farming reached Europe, by contrast, slowly from Southwest Asia.
q-urgeschichte-36#question: Which animal was the first to be domesticated?
q-urgeschichte-36#explanation: The dog was bred from the wolf as early as the Palaeolithic; sheep, goats and cattle followed in the Neolithic, the horse only in the Copper Age.
q-urgeschichte-37#question: In which present-day country did researchers find early evidence of horse keeping in the Botai culture?
q-urgeschichte-37#explanation: Traces of mare's milk in pottery date from around 3500 BC there; genetically, however, today's domestic horses descend from the steppe north of the Black Sea.
q-urgeschichte-38#question: How did the inhabitants of Çatalhöyük enter their houses?
q-urgeschichte-38#choices.1: Over wooden bridges between the houses
q-urgeschichte-38#explanation: The mud-brick houses stood wall to wall without streets; the settlement in Anatolia had up to 8,000 inhabitants at times.
q-urgeschichte-39#question: What did the inhabitants of Neolithic Jericho keep in their houses?
q-urgeschichte-39#choices.3: Clay tablets with their ancestors' names
q-urgeschichte-39#explanation: The plastered skulls point to ancestor worship; Jericho is one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the world.
q-urgeschichte-40#question: Which culture was one of the first to channel river water onto its fields, around 6000 BC?
q-urgeschichte-40#choices.0: The Botai culture in Central Asia
q-urgeschichte-40#choices.3: The Lapita culture in the Pacific
q-urgeschichte-40#explanation: Villages such as Tell es-Sawwan on the middle Tigris and Choga Mami at the edge of the Zagros could thus farm despite little rainfall – a foundation for the later cities of Sumer.
q-urgeschichte-41#question: Why did copper not immediately replace stone as a material?
q-urgeschichte-41#choices.0: It could not be cast in moulds
q-urgeschichte-41#choices.1: It was too soft for many tools
q-urgeschichte-41#choices.2: It was found only in the Americas
q-urgeschichte-41#choices.3: It crumbled in the air within a few years
q-urgeschichte-41#explanation: Copper was prized above all for jewellery, axes and needles; only the harder bronze, made of copper and tin, solved the problem.
q-urgeschichte-42#question: What is the Copper Age cemetery of Varna in Bulgaria famous for?
q-urgeschichte-42#choices.1: The oldest cave paintings in Europe
q-urgeschichte-42#choices.2: The oldest pottery in the world
q-urgeschichte-42#explanation: The graves show how quickly metal became a sign of rank and wealth and how society became more sharply divided into rich and poor.
q-urgeschichte-43#question: In which city is Ötzi on display today?
q-urgeschichte-43#explanation: The glacier mummy is kept in the South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology because the find site at the Tisenjoch lies just inside Italian territory.
q-urgeschichte-44#question: Which metal tool did Ötzi carry with him?
q-urgeschichte-44#explanation: Besides the copper axe he had a bow, arrows, a flint dagger and a backpack frame – a uniquely complete set of equipment from around 3300 BC.
q-urgeschichte-45#choices.1: The coast of the English Channel
q-urgeschichte-45#explanation: The alignment shows how closely Neolithic people observed the course of the year; the great sarsen stones were raised around 2500 BC.
q-urgeschichte-46#question: What does the term megalith refer to?
q-urgeschichte-46#choices.0: A small, finely knapped stone tool
q-urgeschichte-46#choices.3: A large block of stone, used for tombs or stone circles
q-urgeschichte-46#explanation: The word means 'large stone'; megalithic monuments such as Carnac in Brittany or Newgrange in Ireland are found mainly along Europe's Atlantic coast.
q-urgeschichte-47#question: What did the oldest wagon wheels of around 3500 BC look like?
q-urgeschichte-47#explanation: Mounted on axles, they made ox-drawn carts possible; at about the same time the potter's wheel appeared in Mesopotamia.
q-urgeschichte-48#question: What did the 2015 DNA analysis of Kennewick Man show?
q-urgeschichte-48#choices.1: He was closely related to today's Indigenous peoples of the region
q-urgeschichte-48#explanation: After years of legal dispute, the roughly 9,000-year-old man, called the Ancient One by the tribes, was ceremonially reburied in 2017.
q-urgeschichte-49#question: What often provided the larger share of food for hunter-gatherers?
q-urgeschichte-49#choices.0: Hunting big game such as mammoths
q-urgeschichte-49#choices.3: Gathering plants, nuts, eggs and small animals
q-urgeschichte-49#explanation: Women and men shared the work; big-game hunting was risky and unreliable, whereas gathering was a dependable source of food.
q-urgeschichte-50#question: What is the technical term for the New Stone Age?
q-urgeschichte-50#explanation: Neolithic means 'New Stone Age'; Palaeolithic stands for the Old Stone Age, Mesolithic for the Middle Stone Age and Chalcolithic for the Copper Age.
q-urgeschichte-51#question: Which of these islands was settled last by the Lapita seafarers and their descendants?
q-urgeschichte-51#explanation: Lapita seafarers reached Fiji, Tonga and Samoa about 3,000 years ago; New Zealand was not settled until around AD 1250.
q-urgeschichte-52#question: Which of these events happened last?
q-urgeschichte-52#choices.2: The raising of the great sarsen stones at Stonehenge
q-urgeschichte-52#choices.3: The first smelting of copper ore
q-urgeschichte-52#explanation: The order: Çatalhöyük around 7100 BC, copper smelting around 5000 BC, Ötzi's death around 3300 BC and the Stonehenge sarsens around 2500 BC.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-01#question: With which event did the Second World War begin in Europe?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-01#choices.1: The attack on the Soviet Union
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-01#explanation: On September 1, 1939 the Wehrmacht attacked Poland; two days later Great Britain and France declared war on Germany.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-02#question: How many Jews were murdered in the Holocaust?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-02#explanation: The National Socialists murdered around six million European Jews, as well as hundreds of thousands of Sinti and Roma, people with disabilities and other groups.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-03#question: Which battle is regarded as the turning point of the war on the Eastern Front?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-03#explanation: With the surrender of the Sixth Army at Stalingrad in February 1943, the Wehrmacht went permanently on the defensive in the East.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-04#question: What was discussed at the Wannsee Conference in January 1942?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-04#choices.0: The attack on the Soviet Union
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-04#choices.2: The organization of the deportation and murder of the European Jews
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-04#explanation: Under the direction of Reinhard Heydrich, the SS and government ministries coordinated the so-called Final Solution of the Jewish Question.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-05#question: To which resistance group did Sophie and Hans Scholl belong?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-05#explanation: The White Rose distributed leaflets against the Nazi regime in Munich; the Scholl siblings were executed in 1943.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-06#question: Which date is regarded as the end of the Second World War in Europe?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-06#explanation: On May 8, 1945 the unconditional surrender of the Wehrmacht came into force; Japan did not capitulate until September 2.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-07#question: What did Germany and the Soviet Union agree in the secret additional protocol of the Hitler-Stalin Pact of August 1939?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-07#choices.0: A joint attack on Great Britain
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-07#choices.1: The division of Poland and Eastern Europe into spheres of interest
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-07#choices.2: The exchange of prisoners of war
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-07#explanation: The protocol divided Poland along the rivers Narew, Vistula and San and assigned Finland, the Baltic states and Bessarabia to the Soviet sphere.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-08#question: Who set off the bomb at the Wolf's Lair Führer headquarters on July 20, 1944?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-08#explanation: Colonel Stauffenberg placed the briefcase with the explosive at the situation briefing; Hitler survived slightly injured, and Stauffenberg was shot that same night.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-09#question: What happened after the capture of Nanking in December 1937?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-09#choices.0: Japanese troops murdered tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners over a period of weeks
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-09#choices.2: The city was declared the capital of Japan
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-09#choices.3: The League of Nations sent peacekeeping troops
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-09#explanation: The Nanking Massacre lasted about six weeks; the Tokyo Tribunal assumed more than 200,000 dead, and mass rape was part of the crime.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-10#question: Which charge was tried for the first time before an international court at the Nuremberg Trials of 1945/46?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-10#explanation: Alongside war crimes and crimes against peace, the tribunal introduced the new offense of crimes against humanity, which shapes international criminal law to this day.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-11#question: Which territory did Czechoslovakia cede to Germany after the Munich Agreement of 1938?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-11#explanation: Great Britain, France, Italy and Germany agreed, without the participation of Czechoslovakia, on the cession of the largely German-speaking Sudetenland.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-12#question: Which theologian of the Confessing Church was executed at the Flossenbürg concentration camp in April 1945?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-12#explanation: Bonhoeffer had joined the resistance through the Abwehr and was hanged on April 9, 1945 on Hitler's orders; Niemöller survived the Dachau concentration camp.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-13#question: Who appointed Adolf Hitler Reich Chancellor on 30 January 1933?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-13#explanation: As Reich President, Hindenburg had the right to appoint the chancellor. Conservative politicians around Papen believed they could "contain" Hitler in a cabinet with few Nazi ministers. Within a few months he nevertheless established a dictatorship.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-14#question: Which was the only party in the Reichstag to vote against the Enabling Act in March 1933?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-14#explanation: SPD chairman Otto Wels justified the refusal by saying that freedom and life could be taken, but not honour. The KPD deputies had already been arrested or had fled.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-15#question: What did the National Socialists call "Gleichschaltung" (coordination) in 1933/34?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-15#choices.0: The subjugation of state and society to the Nazi Party
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-15#choices.1: Equalising the wages of all workers
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-15#explanation: The states, trade unions, associations, press and culture were dissolved or placed under Nazi leadership. Anyone who did not comply lost their position or was sent to a concentration camp.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#question: What did the Nuremberg Laws of 1935 lay down?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#choices.0: Jews lost full citizenship rights, and marriages with non-Jews were banned
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#choices.1: All Jews had to leave Germany within a year
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#choices.2: Jews had to wear a visible yellow star
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#choices.3: Jews were resettled into ghettos within German cities
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-16#explanation: The laws turned racist ideology into binding law and defined who was regarded as a Jew. The yellow star was only made compulsory in the Reich in 1941.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#question: Which event did the Nazi regime use as a pretext for the November Pogroms of 1938?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#choices.0: The burning of the Reichstag building
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#choices.1: The assassination attempt by a young Jew on a German diplomat in Paris
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#choices.2: An alleged border incident on the Polish border
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#choices.3: The annexation of Austria to the German Reich
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-17#explanation: Seventeen-year-old Herschel Grynszpan, in despair over the deportation of his parents, shot the diplomat Ernst vom Rath. In the pogroms that followed, hundreds of people were murdered or driven to their deaths and some 30,000 Jewish men were taken to concentration camps.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#question: What was the outcome of the international refugee conference at Évian in July 1938?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#choices.0: The participants agreed on sanctions against the German Reich
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#choices.1: Almost no country was willing to take in more Jewish refugees
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#choices.2: Palestine was opened to unlimited Jewish immigration
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#choices.3: The USA doubled its immigration quotas for Germans
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-18#explanation: Representatives of 32 states expressed regret at the fate of the persecuted but hardly opened their borders; only the Dominican Republic offered to admit a larger number.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-19#question: Which country took in about 10,000 Jewish children in 1938/39 through the so-called Kindertransport?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-19#explanation: The children from Germany, Austria, Czechoslovakia and Poland came without their parents. Most of them never saw their families again.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-20#question: Which country was annexed to the German Reich in March 1938?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-20#explanation: After the Wehrmacht marched in, the "Anschluss" was confirmed by a manipulated referendum. Arrests and violent attacks on Jews began immediately, above all in Vienna.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-21#question: Who, acting alone, tried to kill Hitler with a bomb in Munich's Bürgerbräukeller on 8 November 1939?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-21#explanation: The carpenter had spent weeks secretly building the bomb into a pillar on his own; Hitler left the hall 13 minutes before the explosion. Elser was murdered in Dachau concentration camp in April 1945.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#question: What is meant by the term "Blitzkrieg"?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#choices.0: Rapid campaigns in which tanks and aircraft together thrust deep into enemy territory
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#choices.1: Surprise air raids aimed exclusively at large cities
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#choices.2: A war decided by a single naval battle
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#choices.3: Declaring war without prior diplomatic negotiations
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-22#explanation: In this way Poland, France and the Balkans were overrun within weeks between 1939 and 1941. Against the Soviet Union the concept failed, and the war became a long war of attrition.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-23#question: Who became British prime minister on 10 May 1940, the day of the German attack in the west?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-23#explanation: Churchill replaced the appeaser Chamberlain and rejected any compromise peace with Hitler. His speeches strengthened the British will to hold out.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-24#question: From where did Charles de Gaulle call on the French to keep fighting on 18 June 1940?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-24#explanation: De Gaulle spoke on BBC radio and became the leader of Free France. In the occupied country, the Resistance fought against German rule.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-25#question: Who headed the Vichy regime in France, which collaborated with Germany?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-25#explanation: The hero of Verdun concluded the armistice with Germany in 1940. The Vichy regime took part in the deportation of Jews; Pétain was sentenced to death in 1945 and the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-26#question: Where did British experts around Alan Turing break the German Enigma cipher?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-26#explanation: The intelligence gained there, codenamed "Ultra", helped above all in the U-boat battle in the Atlantic. The work remained secret until the 1970s.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-27#question: Under which codename did the German attack on the Soviet Union begin on 22 June 1941?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-27#explanation: With over three million German soldiers it was one of the largest attacks in military history. From the outset it was waged as a war of annihilation against Jews, communists and the Slavic population.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#question: What did the so-called Commissar Order of June 1941 command?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#choices.0: That Soviet commissars be treated especially well as prisoners of war
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#choices.1: That a German commissioner be installed in every occupied village
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#choices.2: That captured political commissars of the Red Army be shot immediately
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#choices.3: That the Wehrmacht be placed under the supervision of party commissars
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-28#explanation: The order deliberately broke international law and shows that the Wehrmacht leadership helped plan and carry out the war of annihilation in the East.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-29#question: At which site near Kyiv did SS and police units murder more than 33,000 Jewish men, women and children within two days at the end of September 1941?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-29#explanation: The massacre in the ravine of Babyn Yar was one of the largest single crimes of the Holocaust. It stands for the mass shootings by Einsatzgruppen behind the Eastern Front, which claimed well over a million victims.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-30#question: Roughly how long did the German siege of Leningrad last?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-30#explanation: The city was encircled from September 1941 to January 1944; the German leadership deliberately sought to starve it. Around one million civilians died, most of them of hunger and cold.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-31#question: How many of the roughly 5.7 million Soviet prisoners of war in German captivity died?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-31#choices.3: About five and a half million
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-31#explanation: They died mainly from deliberate starvation, epidemics and shootings. After the Jews, they were the largest group of victims of Nazi extermination policy.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-32#question: Which mark did Jews in the German Reich have to wear visibly on their clothing from September 1941?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-32#explanation: The yellow star bearing the word "Jude" made the persecuted publicly identifiable and isolated them. A few weeks later the systematic deportations from the Reich to the East began.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-33#question: Against whom was the so-called "Aktion T4" directed from 1940?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-33#choices.3: People with disabilities and mental illnesses
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-33#explanation: In six killing centres some 70,000 patients were murdered with gas by August 1941. After public protest, for instance by Bishop von Galen, the operation was officially stopped, but the killing continued in decentralised form.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-34#question: Which of these camps was a pure extermination camp whose sole purpose was mass murder?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-34#explanation: In 1942/43 well over 700,000 people were murdered at Treblinka, most of them Polish Jews. Dachau, Buchenwald and Sachsenhausen were concentration camps in which tens of thousands also died from labour, hunger and violence.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-35#question: What does the Hebrew word "Shoah", used for the Holocaust, mean?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-35#explanation: Many prefer the term Shoah because the Greek word holocaust originally referred to a completely burnt sacrifice. The Yad Vashem memorial in Jerusalem commemorates those who were murdered.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-36#question: Which Romani term is often used for the genocide of the Sinti and Roma?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-36#explanation: Hundreds of thousands of Sinti and Roma were murdered in Nazi-dominated Europe. The Federal Republic of Germany only officially recognised the crimes as genocide in 1982.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-37#question: Who commanded the Jewish Combat Organisation in the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising of 1943?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-37#explanation: The 24-year-old died in May 1943 in the bunker at 18 Miła Street. Korczak had been deported to Treblinka with the children of his orphanage in 1942, and Ringelblum had created the secret ghetto archive.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-38#question: Where did Danes bring most of their country's Jewish population to safety in October 1943?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-38#explanation: Warned of the planned deportation, fishermen took some 7,000 people by boat across the Øresund to neutral Sweden. As a result, the great majority of Danish Jews survived.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-39#question: In which camp did Anne Frank die in early 1945?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-39#explanation: After the Amsterdam hiding place was discovered in August 1944, she was deported via Westerbork to Auschwitz and then to Bergen-Belsen. There, like her sister Margot, she died of typhus a few weeks before liberation.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#question: Why is 27 January International Holocaust Remembrance Day?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#choices.0: Because the Wannsee Conference took place on that day in 1942
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#choices.1: Because the November Pogroms began on that day in 1938
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#choices.2: Because the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising began on that day in 1943
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#choices.3: Because Auschwitz was liberated on that day in 1945
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-40#explanation: Soviet soldiers found some 7,000 surviving prisoners there. The United Nations declared it an international day of remembrance in 2005; Germany has observed it since 1996.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-41#question: Which British general defeated Rommel's Panzer Army at El Alamein in 1942?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-41#explanation: The Eighth Army's victory in Egypt turned the war in North Africa. In May 1943 the German and Italian troops in Tunisia surrendered.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-42#question: Which symbolic figure represented the women who worked in the US war industry?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-42#explanation: Millions of American women built aircraft, ships and ammunition. The poster with the slogan "We Can Do It!" later became an icon of the women's movement.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-43#question: Under which name did an all-female Soviet night bomber regiment become known?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-43#explanation: The name was given to them by German soldiers. The pilots flew thousands of night missions in slow biplanes; altogether hundreds of thousands of women served in the Red Army.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-44#question: What happened from 1942 onward to about 120,000 people of Japanese descent on the US West Coast?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-44#choices.1: They were sent to internment camps
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-44#choices.2: They were conscripted into the Pacific Fleet
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-44#choices.3: They were permitted to settle in Hawaii
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-44#explanation: About two thirds of them were American citizens. In 1988 the US government formally apologised and paid compensation to the survivors.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#question: Whom does the euphemistic term "comfort women" refer to in the Second World War?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#choices.0: Nurses who cared for wounded soldiers in military hospitals
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#choices.1: Women who wrote to soldiers at the front as pen pals
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#choices.2: Women and girls who were taken to brothels and sexually exploited by the Japanese military
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#choices.3: Chaplains who worked in prisoner-of-war camps
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-45#explanation: Tens of thousands of women, mainly from Korea, China and the Philippines, became victims of this system. From 1991 survivors such as Kim Hak-sun publicly broke their silence.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-46#question: Under which codename did the Western Allies land in Normandy in June 1944?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-46#explanation: On D-Day, 6 June 1944, more than 150,000 soldiers went ashore. Torch was the landing in North Africa in 1942, Husky the one in Sicily in 1943.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-47#question: Where did Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet in February 1945 to discuss the post-war order?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-47#explanation: In the Crimea they agreed on dividing Germany into occupation zones and founding the United Nations. At Potsdam in the summer of 1945, Truman had already taken Roosevelt's place.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-48#question: Who headed the Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda from 1933?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-48#explanation: Goebbels controlled the press, radio, film and culture. The cheap "people's receiver" radio was meant to bring propaganda into every household.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-49#question: What was the name of the Nazi youth organisation for girls?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-49#explanation: The League of German Girls (BDM) was part of the Hitler Youth, membership of which became compulsory in 1939. Girls were above all to be prepared for their role as mothers in line with Nazi ideology.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-50#question: On which city did the USA drop the second atomic bomb on 9 August 1945?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-50#explanation: Hiroshima had been destroyed three days earlier. By the end of 1945, well over 100,000 people had died in the two cities, many from the effects of radiation.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#question: What was special about Emperor Hirohito's radio address of 15 August 1945?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#choices.0: The emperor announced his abdication in it
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#choices.1: The emperor called for a fight to the last man in it
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#choices.2: The people heard their emperor's voice for the first time
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#choices.3: The speech was broadcast live from Washington
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-51#explanation: In the pre-recorded address Hirohito announced the acceptance of the Allied surrender terms without using the word surrender. He remained emperor after the war.
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-52#question: Roughly how many people died in the Second World War?
q-zweiter-weltkrieg-52#explanation: Most of the dead were civilians. With around 27 million victims, the Soviet Union suffered the highest losses of any country.
